title: Drone Strike Hits Residence of Opposition-Aligned General 'Shub' in Doolow, Sparking Turkey-Blame Row
detail: Two missiles struck the Doolow, Gedo region compound of Gen. Mahad Abdirahman Aden ('Taliye Shub'), the former commander of Somalia's Custodial Corps and a military figure aligned with ousted Southwest State president Laftagareen, overnight between September 3 and 4, 2026; a third projectile reportedly landed near the residence of the Doolow district commissioner. Jubbaland's regional administration accused Turkish military aircraft/drones of carrying out the strike and called it a war crime, saying Gen. Shub, his wife and two other family members sustained shrapnel wounds. Casualty figures remain contested: some early reporting described only minor injuries with no deaths, while other outlets reported one to three fatalities, including a domestic worker killed in the compound. Somalia's federal Ministry of Information denied any government or allied involvement, saying preliminary security-agency information indicated the explosions originated from explosives being prepared inside the house rather than an external strike. Former presidents Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo publicly condemned the incident and demanded accountability. Neither Villa Somalia nor Ankara has claimed responsibility.

media.caption: A drone strike hit the Doolow residence of opposition-aligned Gen. Mahad Abdirahman 'Shub', Sep 3-4, 2026
